title: Seal a payment exception family and describe it with a switch

blocks.text: Java 17 can close an exception hierarchy with `sealed`, and Java 21 can then switch over it exhaustively. The page's payment family has two members; this one has a third, `FraudSuspectedException`. Complete the family and describe it.

items: Make `PaymentException` a **sealed** abstract checked exception that permits exactly `CardDeclinedException`, `PaymentTimeoutException` and `FraudSuspectedException` (all `final`).
Write `PaymentDescriber.describe(PaymentException e)` with a pattern-matching `switch` over the family:

blocks.text: When the family is sealed the compiler knows every subtype, so the switch needs no `default` branch, and a member added later makes the switch fail to compile instead of falling into the wrong branch.

cases.says: A declined card is described with its message, and a timeout as "retry later".
The third member of the family gets its own branch; a default branch would describe it as something it is not.
PaymentException is sealed and permits exactly its three subclasses, so the switch needs no default.
Each member of the family is final; a non-sealed member would reopen the hierarchy the switch relies on.

concepts: One base exception per domain lets callers catch the whole family or one member.
A sealed exception family can be handled by a pattern switch with no default branch.
